original_text: Multi-generator dose-response (N=1,730)... critical crossover boundary (o* ~ 0.51-0.55): whenever query-document overlap exceeds 52%, character n-grams consistently outperform whole words; below 52% overlap, whole-word indexing outperforms character n-grams.
corrected_text: Multi-generator dose-response suite (N=1,930, comprising 1,224 GPT-4o-mini, 400 human-authored, and 306 Qwen2.5-7B queries)... under aggressive entity-substituting paraphrases, word indexing outperforms character n-grams below ~65% lexical overlap (0.4334 vs. 0.2427), whereas under authentic human formulation where entity anchors persist, character and word BM25 perform comparably across all overlap levels (MRRs 0.555-0.577).
rationale: Query count updated from 1,730 to 1,930 (accounting for both verbatim and paraphrase human queries). Crossover framed as generator-dependent artifact of entity substitution rather than an invariant universal boundary.

rationale: Strictly decouples automated document QA (N=150, ANLS/EM) from genuine human evaluation of personal photo albums and relational retrieval (N=110, kappa = 0.9031). Quarantines simulated rater code.
